name: Large power transformers & switchgear
description_md: Every gigawatt of data-center load needs large power transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, and substation gear — a market that was sized for ~1% annual load growth and is now asked to double output. Lead times for large transformers average 115-130 weeks (up to four years without a reservation), and the top makers are booked years out: Hitachi Energy, the world's largest transformer maker, carries a backlog above $43B (vs ~$14B three years earlier) and its CEO has publicly warned of shortage; HD Hyundai Electric has more than three years of production booked (~$7.9B backlog); Siemens Energy's Grid Technologies backlog hit a record €51B; Eaton — data centers now its largest end-market — bought Boyd Thermal for $9.5B to sell 'grid-to-chip'. Factories to relieve the squeeze (Hitachi's $4.5B program, US plants) do not add meaningful output before ~2027-28 because a transformer plant itself takes years to build and staff. Status basis: judged binding — multi-year lead times on a non-substitutable, code-required component sit directly on every substation in every utility queue.

controlled_by.share_note: World's largest transformer maker; >$43B backlog, multi-year lead times (company_claimed via press)
Leading MV switchgear/power distribution; data centers its largest end-market; $9.5B Boyd Thermal deal closed Mar 2026 (company_pr)
>3 years of production booked, ~$7.9B backlog on US DC/grid orders (press_reported)

dependents.dependency_md: The ~40GW NoVA pipeline is executed substation by substation; each requires large transformers ordered years ahead — utility energization dates inherit transformer lead times.
Developer delivery schedules depend on long-lead electrical gear; developers now pre-order transformers/switchgear speculatively and carry them as inventory to protect timelines.
Grid and substation construction backlog ($48.5B) can only convert to revenue as owner-furnished transformers and switchgear arrive on site.
In-building power distribution (switchgear, busway, PDUs) shares component supply chains; Vertiv's ~$15B backlog reflects the same gear scarcity one tier down.

substitutes_md: Essentially none for large power transformers — they are engineered-to-order, code-required, and only a dozen global plants make the largest classes. Mitigations: reconditioned/used units (thin market), standardizing designs to enable batch orders, on-site generation to defer grid gear, and higher-voltage direct designs (800VDC inside the DC reduces some downstream gear but not the grid-side transformer). New entrants and US plant expansions (Hitachi $4.5B incl. ~$500M North America; Korean and Powell/Hyosung capacity) arrive 2027+. Amorphous-core and dry-type alternatives serve smaller ratings only.
downcycle_md: Transformer makers are unusually downturn-resistant this cycle: backlogs are 3-4+ years deep, diversified across utilities/renewables/industrial (data centers are ~20% or less of most books), and orders carry deposits and escalation clauses — Hitachi's >$43B and HD Hyundai's 3-year book would cushion even a sharp AI pullback, with cancellations landing first on speculative developer pre-orders rather than utility programs. The glut risk is timing: capacity built for the 2026 panic arriving into a softer 2029 market, repeating the industry's post-1970s overcapacity trauma that caused today's underinvestment. Switchgear (shorter-cycle, more DC-exposed, e.g. Eaton/Vertiv books) would feel a demand fall several quarters before transformers.

observations.method_md: Midpoint of the 115-130-week average large-transformer lead time reported by POWER Magazine; unreserved orders quoted up to 48 months.
